findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem rendered inside .map() without a key prop
findings.body: In FilterView.tsx the map over `rules` renders `GrafanaRuleListItem` for the `grafana` origin without a `key` prop, while the sibling `datasource` case still passes `key={key}`. The pre-existing code (deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader`) was passed `key={key}`; the replacement JSX drops that attribute. React relies on a stable key per list child to reconcile the list — without it React will warn in console and may reuse/mis-render state when rules are reordered, filtered, or partially updated. Add `key={key}` to the `GrafanaRuleListItem` JSX, mirroring the dataSource branch.

findings.title: Tests mock the wrong ability hook for RuleActionsButtons (stale comment and mocks)
findings.body:
The mock table and all assertions are built around `useAlertRuleAbility` (singular), with the comment 'RuleActionsButtons uses: useAlertRuleAbility (singular)'. After this PR, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` no longer calls `useAlertRuleAbility` — it calls `useRulerRuleAbility` for the ruler-side edit ability and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility` (with `skipToken`) for the prom-side fallback. As a result the per-test overrides of `useAlertRuleAbility` (e.g. for Update/Delete) have no effect on what is rendered, and the previous default `[false, false]` from `useRulerRuleAbility` is what actually drives `canEditRule`/`canDelete` etc. Concretely:

- The 'Should not render Delete button for users without the delete permission' test never sets `useRulerRuleAbility`/`useRulerRuleAbilities` for Grafana, so it appears to pass for the wrong reason (and only because the grafana-side plural hook is overridden); it does not exercise the OR-of-abilities logic in `AlertRuleMenu`.
- The 'Should render Delete button for users with the delete permission' test depends on the same gap.

Update the mocks and the explanatory comment so that the singular/plural ruler and grafana-prom hooks used by the V2 components are what is being stubbed, and assert against the actual hook calls. Otherwise a regression in `useRulerRuleAbility`/abilities OR'ing would go undetected.

findings.title: Pause and Delete menu items are silently unavailable in the list view (rulerRule is now undefined)
findings.body:
`AlertRuleMenu` still gates the Pause and Delete entries on the presence of the ruler-side data:

- Pause: `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && groupIdentifier.groupOrigin === 'grafana' && (<MenuItemPauseRule rule={rulerRule} ... />)}`
- Delete: `{canDelete && rulerRule && (... onClick={() => handleDelete(rulerRule, groupIdentifier)} ...)}`

After this PR the grafana list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem`, `FilterView`) constructs the actions tree with only `promRule`, so `rulerRule` is `undefined` everywhere and both menu items disappear — not because the user lacks permissions (the abilities are still `[supported, allowed]` via the grafana-prom fallback) but because the underlying click handlers need the full ruler payload. This is a behavior regression vs. the previous list view and is not described in the PR description. Users will have to drill into each rule's detail page to pause or delete it, and any bulk operations built on the list will also break. Either plumb through enough ruler data (or use a prom-based delete path) so these actions keep working in the list, or call out this UX change explicitly and gate the entire removal behind a feature flag.

findings.title: Dropping ruler fallback loses the 'Creating' / 'Deleting' rule states
findings.body:
Before this change `GrafanaGroupLoader` fetched ruler data, paired it with the prom response via `matchRules`, and rendered outstanding rulers with `RuleOperation.Creating` and unmatched prom rules with `RuleOperation.Deleting`. After removing the ruler fetch (and `matchRules`/`RulerRuleLoadingError`), the component only renders `promResponse.data.groups.at(0)?.rules` directly. As a consequence:

- A rule that has been accepted by the ruler but not yet propagated to Prometheus (window of eventual consistency) disappears from the list instead of being shown with the 'Creating' badge.
- A rule that has been deleted from the ruler but is still in the prom response no longer appears as 'Deleting'.

Previously these intermediates were explicitly logged with `logWarning` because they are rare/expected; now they are silently absent, hiding the operation from the user. Either keep the ruler fetch + match (same call it makes today) just for status derivation, or update the prom API so the rule DTO carries a creation/in-flight marker that the list can render without a second query. This should be flagged in the PR description and either preserved or have tests covering the in-flight state.
